areas.area: 3. Permissions, multi-tenant, and API ID tampering

scenarios.title: Concurrent requests cannot double-book one slot or leave a partial group
scenarios.risk: Two customers may receive the same resource/time or a partial group may persist.

scenarios.title: Idempotency-Key replays the original successful booking outcome

establishedFailure.problem: Duplicate-safe 201+409 conflict handling is not an idempotent replay contract.
establishedFailure.reproduction: Send the same POST /api/appointments or POST /api/booking-groups request twice with the same Idempotency-Key after the first 201 response.
establishedFailure.risk: Clients retrying after a transport failure receive 409 instead of a stable replayable result and cannot safely distinguish a completed booking from a conflict.
establishedFailure.cause: Code review established that booking endpoints ignore Idempotency-Key; duplicate prevention relies on slot-conflict handling, producing 201 then 409 rather than idempotent replay.
establishedFailure.solution: Add a tenant- and customer-scoped durable idempotency record keyed by endpoint, Idempotency-Key and canonical request hash; atomically store and replay the original completed response, rejecting key reuse with a different payload.
establishedFailure.proposedSolution: Add the idempotency record inside the booking transaction, retain it through the retry window, and add isolated replay/concurrency tests before enabling it.

scenarios.evidence: Established code-review finding: Code review established that booking endpoints ignore Idempotency-Key; duplicate prevention relies on slot-conflict handling, producing 201 then 409 rather than idempotent replay.

scenarios.title: Lost response/process restart can reconcile a booking command to its durable outcome

establishedFailure.problem: A booking command has no durable client-reconcilable terminal outcome after response loss or process restart.
establishedFailure.reproduction: Submit a booking, drop the client response or restart the API after commit, then retry or query using the original command identifier.
establishedFailure.affectedSystem: Public booking API command handling and durable booking storage
establishedFailure.risk: A client cannot deterministically recover whether an accepted booking committed; retries can surface a conflict without the original appointment outcome.
establishedFailure.cause: Code review established there is no durable command/outcome record or reconciliation endpoint for booking requests after a lost response or process restart.
establishedFailure.solution: Persist a command ID, canonical request hash and terminal appointment/group outcome in the same transaction; expose authenticated reconciliation and replay by command ID.
